title: Life strategies of loneliness among older people: Constructs for developing a psychological diagnostic tool for assessing levels of experience
abstract: Context and relevance. The acceleration of population aging on a global scale and the complex of socio-psychological problems caused by this process actualize the creation of a methodological basis for positive life strategies for the elderly and a radical revision of existing psychological diagnoses, taking into account their reorientation to a prosperous old age. Objective. The aim of this study is to provide a theoretical justification for the conceptual framework of psychological diagnostics of the levels of experiencing loneliness among elderly people, from the perspective of the prospects for its application in developing positive life strategies for addressing loneliness among elderly people. Methods and materials. The methodological basis of the study consists of the ideas and concepts of scholars related to the experience of loneliness in older adults, which made it possible to build a theoretical foundation for developing a life strategy for addressing loneliness. In the development and implementation of the diagnostic process, the following approaches were used: a cognitive approach — to assess cognitive distortions and define diagnostic criteria; a psychodynamic approach — to develop diagnostics for measuring experiences of loneliness; an existential approach — to carry out differential diagnostics; ideas from symbolic interactionism and radical constructivism — to construct criteria and indicators of the levels of experiencing loneliness; and conceptual modeling of the levels of experiencing loneliness. Results. The theoretical foundations and key concepts of the life strategy of loneliness have been developed, aimed at improving diagnostic procedures for psychologists in terms of developing life strategies for older people, assessing their readiness to overcome difficulties in the social sphere, supporting the consciously chosen strategy of dealing with loneliness, correcting maladaptive states, and preventing risks associated with extreme forms of experiencing loneliness. The criteria and levels of experiencing loneliness by older people have been identified in relation to the choice of life strategies and taking into account the “successful” and “unsuccessful” types of aging. Conclusions. Theoretical generalizations and the author’s conceptual framework for psychological diagnostics of the levels of experiencing loneliness are applicable for the development of positive life strategies and programs of psychological support and assistance for older people.
